messages:
liam: I dropped a tiny sampleapp demonstrating a 'checkpoint-and-reattach' flow for the Go Generator SDK. looking for API ergonomics feedback
frank: can you paste the link/snippet?
liam: repo: https://git.redwood/internal/sampleapps/gen-checkpoint. core idea: keep a checkpoint token and reattach after a detach without replaying already-processed parts. snippet: 
```go
ctx := context.Background()
sess := client.Generators.Start(ctx, cfg)
for p := range sess.Stream() {
  handle(p)
  sess.SetCheckpoint(p.Seq)
}
if sess.Interrupted() {
  rctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
  defer cancel()
  resumed, err := client.Generators.ResumeWithCheckpoint(rctx, sess.ID, sess.CheckpointToken())
  // resumed.Stream() should continue after checkpoint
}
```
nora: nice write-up. FYI we hit flakes in CI where callers reused a request-scoped ctx for Resume and got ErrDeadlineExceeded immediately. that's a real footgun.
frank: UX options: (A) document explicitly "use a fresh ctx for Resume"; (B) Resume(ctx, opts) with HandshakeTimeout; (C) add sess.Reattach(ctx) helper that does its own bounded handshake and returns resumed stream + meta.
liam: i'm leaning to Reattach helper: hides the handshake detail so users don't accidentally reuse expired ctxs. proposed signature: Reattach(ctx) (Stream, resumed bool, error).
nora: plus: server-driven detaches are currently mapped to io.EOF client-side, so apps can't tell normal completion vs auth rotate. propose ErrStreamDetached sentinel and Stream.DetachMeta() returning a code like "auth_rotate" or "server_restart".
frank: agree. also, server Resume should be idempotent and accept checkpoint + replay-protection token; if conflict, return 409 -> SDK translate to ErrReplayConflict. add metrics gen.resume.path and gen.resume.replay_conflicts.
